title: The Co-Design Future: Scaling AI from Data Centers to the Edge
description: This discussion focuses on AMD's strategy, system co-design across the entire data center, and the emerging landscape of agentic workloads. It highlights the need for integrated hardware solutions and the necessary management and security layers for distributed AI inference.
summary: The presentation details AMD's accelerating market position, driven by strong adoption of Epic and the momentum of their CPU family, Venice, which is designed for the agentic era and leverages x86 compatibility. A core theme is the necessity of co-designing the entire data center—including CPUs, GPUs, memory, networking, and power—to maximize efficiency and performance. The discussion emphasizes the partnership with Cerebrus to deliver fully integrated systems, enabling unmatched speed and low latency. Enterprise customers are seeing significant ROI and are shifting towards agentic deployments, requiring predictable infrastructure and token cost management. Looking forward, AI inference will be distributed beyond the data center to edge and desktop devices, necessitating sophisticated management planes (like Cisco Cloud Control) for monitoring agent behavior, ensuring safety, and containing token consumption across the entire computing estate.

title: The Future of AI: From Agentic Computing to Personal and Physical Intelligence
description: This talk explores the radical shift in AI, moving from traditional LLMs to agentic AI and the necessary evolution of compute infrastructure. It outlines a strategy for building an open ecosystem that powers the next era of AI everywhere, encompassing personal, enterprise, and physical applications.
summary: The speaker discusses the incredible acceleration of AI, noting that the shift from basic LLMs to agentic AI is creating an entirely new demand for compute, particularly for CPUs, which are essential for running distributed, complex agent systems. The company’s strategy centers on compute leadership and building an open ecosystem to provide the right compute for the right workload. A key focus is extending AI beyond the data center into personal and physical applications (Personal AI and Physical AI), where agents sense the world and take action to amplify human potential. The speaker concludes by previewing future products, including new CPU architecture, to deliver a unified platform for building and deploying intelligent systems across all environments.

title: MI455 Performance and Scaling Roadmap: Driving Generational Leaps in AI Throughput
description: This discussion details the significant performance gains of the MI455 accelerator compared to prior generations, emphasizing massive throughput improvements and the strategic roadmap for future scaling (MI500, MI600). It also highlights the role of optimized training techniques and key partnerships that drive the AI ecosystem forward.
summary: The discussion centers on the exceptional performance of the MI455, which achieves four times the throughput of the MI355 at lower concurrency and up to 34 times more throughput with Helios at the highest concurrency. Performance is further boosted by training optimizations like fused flash attention, leading to 2.4 times better training performance. Strategically, the company is focused on ecosystem readiness, highlighted by the Rockem.ai Day 0 support for MI455 and the deployment of models like DeepSeek V4 Pro on Helios. The future roadmap includes the MI4-30X, which is foundational for sovereign AI factories, and next-generation chips like the MI500 and MI600, aiming to deliver massive leaps in inference throughput (potentially over 2,000 times higher) through scaling and next-generation architectures. Major partnerships, such as the one involving the MI300, are also key to the overall strategy.

title: The Exponential Acceleration of AI Demand: Scaling Compute and the Shift to Inference
description: This segment highlights the massive, accelerating demand for AI, demonstrated by 158x token consumption growth and 5x annual increases in training compute. It details the critical shift toward inference, the projected growth of the accelerator market, and the specialized role of high-performance CPUs in meeting modern AI workloads.
summary: The video illustrates the exponential growth of AI demand, marked by a 158x increase in monthly token consumption over two years and training FLOPS increasing fivefold every year since 2020, indicating a rapidly steepening demand curve. A key shift is the move toward inference, with projections showing that by 2026, over 60% of global AI compute capacity will be dedicated to inference. This acceleration is driving the AI accelerator market toward $1.4 trillion by 2030. The discussion then shifts to hardware, emphasizing the role of CPUs (like Epic/Venice) in feeding GPUs, with the CPU portfolio designed to optimize both GPU servers and general-purpose enterprise workloads. Specific hardware advantages include high-density performance, superior per-core performance (20% higher than competitors), and the flexibility to handle diverse needs across different AI workloads. Finally, the segment notes that smaller, highly capable models are rapidly closing the gap in frontier performance, making advanced AI accessible on personal systems.

title: AMD's Strategy for the AI-Infused Computing Ecosystem
description: This session outlines AMD's strategy to capture the massive AI computing market by combining high-performance hardware with an open software ecosystem. Key focus areas include leveraging AI-assisted development tools, open-source models, and next-generation AI hardware architectures.
summary: The presentation focused on AMD's vision for the future of AI computing, emphasizing the need for open standards and the massive market potential for high-performance computing. A major focus was the synergy between hardware and software, specifically highlighting how AI is acting as a force multiplier in accelerating progress. AMD introduced Rockum.AI, an agentic platform that uses AI to assist developers in optimizing GPU programming, and detailed the collaboration on LLVM code generation and low-level kernel optimization. Strategically, AMD is driving the open-source AI ecosystem by training and launching advanced models (OTel 2.0) on AMD hardware, positioning the company as a leader in open-source models for the telecom industry. Finally, the session unveiled the new AMD Crea AI system, showcasing the architecture designed to handle intelligence, motion, and safety in next-generation robotics.

title: Co-designing the Future: Deep Hardware-Software Partnerships for Next-Generation AI Ecosystems
description: This discussion highlights a successful, multi-year partnership focused on co-designing next-generation hardware and software solutions for AI workloads. The collaboration emphasizes leveraging deep collaboration on hardware architecture, model training, and system security to unlock future system capabilities.
summary:
The discussion focused on the success and vision of a deep, multi-year partnership centered on co-designing AI infrastructure. Key points include:

**Partnership and Strategy:**
*   The partnership is characterized by bringing together the best talent and resources to lead the industry.
*   The core strategy involves deep collaboration between hardware and software teams to ensure chips and systems are optimized for specific workloads.
*   The goal is to work together on the future, moving beyond simply deploying off-the-shelf solutions.

**Hardware and Co-design:**
*   The teams emphasize the importance of co-designing and co-creating systems (covering aspects like power and cooling) rather than treating hardware as a single component.
*   Specific examples include evaluating hardware platforms (like MI355) and co-designing components (Instinct, Epic, Pensando chips).
*   The ultimate goal is to co-design today for optimal performance in future systems (2028).

**Execution and Impact:**
*   The partnership has led to significant achievements, including the deployment of up to 6 gigawatts of AMD infrastructure and the use of MI455 racks.
*   The process is praised for its ease and productivity, allowing teams to quickly provide insight into workload needs, model requirements, and system responses.

**Software and Security:**
*   Collaboration extends to the software side, focusing on how to train models and manage them across an enterprise.
*   A critical component is ensuring overall safety and security from an apparatus perspective, enabling confidence in the entire deployment and management stack.

title: Helios: The Best AI Rack with Superior Performance and Value
description: This discussion highlights the performance advantages of the Helios rack, emphasizing its superior throughput, cost efficiency, and strong ecosystem, positioning it as the leading solution for high-throughput AI workloads. Future plans involve aggressive scaling and close collaboration with researchers to advance ultra-low latency inference.
summary: The Helios system is presented as the best AI rack in the world, built on an open ecosystem utilizing the Ultra Ethernet standard and featuring six volcano nicks and dedicated networking trays to connect 75 GPUs. Performance metrics show that Helios delivers 10-15% more performance than competitors in high-throughput and inference workloads, offering up to 30% more tokens per dollar. Customer demand is extremely strong, leading to plans for massive scale deployment starting late this year and acceleration through 2027. A key innovation is the marriage of the Instinct/Helios architecture with the Cerebrus wafer scaling engine, which provides five times the throughput while maintaining speed. AMD is developing a complete cadence of rack scale systems, with a new Helios system expected annually, and is actively collaborating with researchers to push the boundaries of ultra-low latency inference.
